section.content: Methods and apparatus for collecting data for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) training and performance may include a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) configured to perform and record various measurements. The WTRU may be configured to perform a recording of beam/cell measurements for one or more cells while in a connected state. The configuration may include conditions for determining when to start/stop recording, cell/beam identification to be recorded, conditions for determining which measurements are to be included in the recording. The WTRU may be configured to perform measurement logging, send an indication of the availability of logged measurements, and send a report under certain conditions.

用于收集用于人工智能(AI)和机器学习(ML)训练和性能的数据的方法和设备可包括：无线传送/接收单元(WTRU)，被配置为执行并且记录各种测量。WTRU可被配置为在处于连接状态的同时执行一个或多个小区的波束/小区测量的记录。该配置可包括用于确定何时开始/停止记录的条件、将要被记录的小区/波束标识、用于确定哪些测量结果将要被包括在记录中的条件。WTRU可被配置为执行测量记录，发送关于所记录测量的可用性的指示，并且在某种条件下发送报告。

Data collection enhancement for artificial intelligence and machine learningCross Reference to Related Applications

The present application claims the benefit of U.S. provisional patent application No. 63/456,841 filed 4/2023, the entire contents of which are incorporated herein by reference.

Background

A network or User Equipment (UE) (also referred to as a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU)) using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and/or Machine Learning (ML) based functions relies on data (e.g., radio quality measurements, quality of experience (QoE), measurements such as throughput, delay/latency, buffer level, etc.) for model training and performance monitoring.

Disclosure of Invention

In various exemplary embodiments described herein, the WTRU may be configured to perform and record various measurements to facilitate the collection of data for AI/ML training and performance. WTRUs that use AI-and/or ML-based functions may rely on data measurements such as, for example, radio quality measurements, quality of service (QoS), quality of experience (QoE), throughput measurements, delay measurements, latency measurements, buffer levels, and so forth. The measurements may be used for model training. The measurements may be used for performance monitoring. The WTRU may be configured to perform a recording of beam/cell measurements for one or more cells, where the configuration may include conditions for determining when to start/stop the recording, cell/beam identities to be recorded, conditions for determining which measurements are to be included in the recording (e.g., conditions for determining whether to record an entry), perform the measurement recording, send an indication of the availability of the recorded measurements, and send a report, etc., under certain conditions (e.g., receiving a request/grant from the network), or any suitable combination thereof.

In various examples, as will become apparent in the context of the description herein, to accomplish data collection for AI/ML, a WTRU may be configured to perform and record measurements for a given beam. The WTRU may be configured to determine a cell quality for recording, the cell quality taking into account all detected beams of the cell. The WTRU may be configured to perform the recording under certain conditions (e.g., certain battery level, certain UL/DL throughput, certain data inactivity level, in certain mobility state, etc.). The WTRU may be configured to record a beam/cell measurement if the quality of the beam/cell differs from a previously recorded measurement by a certain value/percentage. The WTRU may be configured to perform the recording based on the WTRU location and/or the WTRU actions being taken or expected to be taken. The WTRU may be configured to perform measurements/recordings according to the first measurement/recording configuration prior to taking or anticipating taking action. The WTRU may be configured to perform the measurement/recording according to the second measurement/recording configuration after taking the action.

An example method for data measurement and recording may be performed by a WTRU. The method may include performing measurements of at least one measurement object associated with at least one beam of at least one cell. While the WTRU is in a connected state, the method may include recording the at least one measurement, wherein the recording may be based on at least one condition. And the method may include transmitting an indication that the at least one recorded measurement is available. The method may further include transmitting a report including the at least one recorded measurement. In response to a request from the network, a report may be sent. The at least one condition may include when to start and stop recording. The at least one condition may include an identification of at least one cell for recording. The at least one condition may include an identification of at least one beam for recording. The at least one condition may include an indication of at least one measurement object for recording.

An exemplary WTRU configured to measure and record data may include a transceiver and a processor. The WTRU may be configured to perform measurements of at least one measurement object associated with at least one beam of at least one cell. While in the connected state, the WTRU may record the at least one measurement, wherein the recording is based on at least one condition. And the WTRU may send an indication via the transceiver that the at least one recorded measurement is available. The WTRU may be further configured to send a report including the at least one recorded measurement via the transceiver. In response to a request from the network, a report may be sent. The at least one condition may include when to start and stop recording. The at least one condition may include an identification of at least one cell for recording. The at least one condition may include an identification of at least one beam for recording. The at least one condition may include an indication of at least one measurement object for recording.

An exemplary computer readable storage medium may have stored thereon executable instructions that, when executed by a processor, cause the processor to perform measurements of at least one measurement object associated with at least one beam of at least one cell. While in the connected state, the processor may record the at least one measurement, wherein the recording is based on at least one condition. And the processor may be configured to send an indication that the at least one recorded measurement is available. The processor may be further configured to send a report comprising the at least one recorded measurement. In response to a request from the network, a report may be sent. The at least one condition may include when to start and stop recording. The at least one condition may include an identification of at least one cell for recording. The at least one condition may include an identification of at least one beam for recording. The at least one condition may include an indication of at least one measurement object for recording.

An exemplary WTRU configured to perform data measurement and logging may include a memory and a processor. The processor may be configured to receive a configuration related to measurement logging and reporting. The configuration may include at least one first condition for starting recording measurements in the memory and at least one second condition for stopping recording measurements in the memory. The at least one first condition may relate to a likelihood of occurrence of at least one first event within a first time period. The at least one second condition may relate to a likelihood that at least one second event has occurred within a second time period. The processor may be configured to perform a first measurement. The processor may be configured to begin recording the second measurement in the memory in response to the first measurement indicating that the likelihood of the at least one first event occurring within the first period of time is at or above a first threshold. The processor may be configured to stop recording the second measurement in the memory based on determining that the likelihood that the at least one second event has occurred within the second time period is above a second threshold. The processor may be configured to send a report comprising an indication of the recorded second measurement. The processor may be configured to send the report in response to determining that a third condition for reporting the measurement is met, wherein the third condition relates to a likelihood of occurrence of at least one third event. In response to a request from the network, a report may be sent. The at least one first condition may comprise an identification of the at least one configured cell for recording. The at least one first event may be based on a location of the WTRU. The likelihood of occurrence of at least one of the at least one first event or the at least one second event may be based on an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model. The first measurement may comprise a quality of the cell. The first measurement may include a quality of the beam. The processor may be configured to delete the first measurement from the memory in response to the first measurement indicating that the likelihood of the at least one first event occurring within the first period of time is below a threshold. The processor may be configured to record in memory a logical identifier associated with an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model.

The configuration may include at least one first condition for starting recording measurements in the memory and at least one second condition for stopping recording measurements in the memory. The at least one first condition may relate to a likelihood of occurrence of at least one first event within a first time period. The at least one second condition may relate to a likelihood that at least one second event has occurred within a second time period. The method may include performing a first measurement. The method may include beginning to record a second measurement in memory in response to the first measurement indicating that the likelihood of the at least one first event occurring within the first period of time is at or above a first threshold. The method may include ceasing to record the second measurement in the memory based on determining that the likelihood that the at least one second event has occurred within the second time period is above a second threshold. The method may include sending a report in response to determining that a third condition for reporting measurements is satisfied, wherein the third condition relates to a likelihood of occurrence of at least one third event. In response to a request from the network, a report may be sent. The at least one first condition may comprise an identification of the at least one configured cell for recording. The at least one first event may be based on a location of the WTRU. The likelihood of occurrence of at least one of the at least one first event or the at least one second event may be based on an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model. The first measurement may comprise a quality of the cell. The first measurement may include a quality of the beam. The method may include recording in memory a logical identifier associated with an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model.

An exemplary computer readable storage medium may have stored thereon executable instructions that, when executed by a processor, cause the processor to perform data measurements and recording. The executable instructions may cause the processor to receive a configuration related to measurement logging and reporting. The configuration may include at least one first condition for starting recording measurements in the memory and at least one second condition for stopping recording measurements in the memory. The at least one first condition may relate to a likelihood of occurrence of at least one first event within a first time period. The at least one second condition may relate to a likelihood that at least one second event has occurred within a second time period. The executable instructions may cause the processor to stop recording the second measurement in the memory based on determining that the likelihood that the at least one second event has occurred within the second time period is above a second threshold. The executable instructions may cause the processor to send a report including an indication of the recorded second measurement. The executable instructions may cause the processor to send a report in response to determining that a third condition for reporting measurements is satisfied, wherein the third condition relates to a likelihood of occurrence of at least one third event. In response to a request from the network, a report may be sent. The at least one first condition may comprise an identification of the at least one configured cell for recording. The at least one first event may be based on a location of the WTRU. The likelihood of occurrence of at least one of the at least one first event or the at least one second event may be based on an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model. The executable instructions may cause the processor to record in memory a logical identifier associated with an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model.

Detailed Description

Exemplary network for implementing the invention

Fig. 1A is a diagram illustrating an exemplary communication system 100 in which one or more disclosed embodiments may be implemented. Communication system 100 may be a multiple-access system that provides content, such as voice, data, video, messaging, broadcast, etc., to a plurality of wireless users. Communication system 100 may enable multiple wireless users to access such content through the sharing of system resources, including wireless bandwidth. For example, communication system 100 may employ one or more channel access methods such as Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA), time Division Multiple Access (TDMA), frequency Division Multiple Access (FDMA), orthogonal FDMA (OFDMA), single carrier FDMA (SC-FDMA), zero-tail unique word DFT spread OFDM (ZT UW DTS-s OFDM), unique word OFDM (UW-OFDM), resource block filtered OFDM, filter Bank Multicarrier (FBMC), and the like.

As shown in fig. 1A, the communication system 100 may include wireless transmit/receive units (WTRUs) 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d, RANs 104/113, CNs 106/115, public Switched Telephone Networks (PSTN) 108, the internet 110, and other networks 112, although it will be understood that the disclosed embodiments contemplate any number of WTRUs, base stations, networks, and/or network elements. Each of the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d may be any type of device configured to operate and/or communicate in a wireless environment. As an example, the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d (any of which may be referred to as a "station" and/or "STA") may be configured to transmit and/or receive wireless signals and may include User Equipment (UE), mobile stations, fixed or mobile subscriber units, subscription-based units, pagers, cellular telephones, personal Digital Assistants (PDAs), smartphones, laptop computers, netbooks, personal computers, wireless sensors, hotspots or Mi-Fi devices, internet of things (IoT) devices, watches or other wearable devices, head-mounted displays (HMDs), vehicles, robots, medical devices and applications (e.g., tele-surgery), industrial devices and applications (e.g., robots and/or other wireless devices operating in an industrial and/or automated processing chain context), consumer electronics devices, devices operating on commercial and/or industrial wireless networks, and the like. Any of the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, and 102d may be interchangeably referred to as a UE.

Communication system 100 may also include base station 114a and/or base station 114b. Each of the base stations 114a, 114b may be any type of device configured to wirelessly interface with at least one of the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d to facilitate access to one or more communication networks (such as the CN 106/115, the internet 110, and/or the other network 112). As an example, the base stations 114a, 114B may be base station transceivers (BTSs), node-bs, eNode bs, home Node bs, home eNode bs, gnbs, NR Node bs, site controllers, access Points (APs), wireless routers, and the like. Although the base stations 114a, 114b are each depicted as a single element, it will be appreciated that the base stations 114a, 114b may include any number of interconnected base stations and/or network elements.

Base station 114a may be part of RAN 104/113 and RAN 104/113 may also include other base stations and/or network elements (not shown), such as a Base Station Controller (BSC), a Radio Network Controller (RNC), a relay node, and the like. Base station 114a and/or base station 114b may be configured to transmit and/or receive wireless signals on one or more carrier frequencies, which may be referred to as cells (not shown). These frequencies may be in a licensed spectrum, an unlicensed spectrum, or a combination of licensed and unlicensed spectrum. A cell may provide coverage of wireless services to a particular geographic area, which may be relatively fixed or may vary over time. The cell may be further divided into cell sectors. For example, a cell associated with base station 114a may be divided into three sectors. Thus, in one embodiment, the base station 114a may include three transceivers, i.e., one for each sector of the cell. In an embodiment, the base station 114a may employ multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology and may use multiple transceivers for each sector of a cell. For example, beamforming may be used to transmit and/or receive signals in desired spatial directions.

The base stations 114a, 114b may communicate with one or more of the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d via an air interface 116, which may be any suitable wireless communication link (e.g., radio Frequency (RF), microwave, centimeter wave, millimeter wave, infrared (IR), ultraviolet (UV), visible light, etc.). The air interface 116 may be established using any suitable Radio Access Technology (RAT).

More specifically, as described above, communication system 100 may be a multiple access system and may employ one or more channel access schemes, such as CDMA, TDMA, FDMA, OFDMA, SC-FDMA, or the like. For example, a base station 114a in the RAN 104/113 and the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c may implement a radio technology, such as Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS) terrestrial radio Access (UTRA), that may use Wideband CDMA (WCDMA) to establish the air interfaces 115/116/117.WCDMA may include communication protocols such as High Speed Packet Access (HSPA) and/or evolved HSPA (hspa+). HSPA may include high speed Downlink (DL) packet access (HSDPA) and/or High Speed UL Packet Access (HSUPA).

In an embodiment, the base station 114a and the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c may implement a radio technology, such as evolved UMTS terrestrial radio access (E-UTRA), which may use Long Term Evolution (LTE) and/or LTE-Advanced (LTE-a) and/or LTE-Advanced Pro (LTE-a Pro) to establish the air interface 116.

In an embodiment, the base station 114a and the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c may implement a radio technology, such as NR radio access, that may use a New Radio (NR) to establish the air interface 116.

In an embodiment, the base station 114a and the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c may implement multiple radio access technologies. For example, the base station 114a and the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c may implement LTE radio access and NR radio access together using, for example, the Dual Connectivity (DC) principle. Thus, the air interface used by the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c may be characterized by multiple types of radio access technologies and/or transmissions to/from multiple types of base stations (e.g., enbs and gnbs).

In other embodiments, the base station 114a and the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c may implement radio technologies such as IEEE 802.11 (i.e., wireless fidelity (WiFi)), IEEE 802.16 (i.e., worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX)), CDMA2000 1X, CDMA EV-DO, transitional standard 2000 (IS-2000), transitional standard 95 (IS-95), transitional standard 856 (IS-856), global system for mobile communications (GSM), enhanced data rates for GSM evolution (EDGE), GSM EDGE (GERAN), and the like.

The base station 114B in fig. 1A may be, for example, a wireless router, a home Node B, a home eNode B, or an access point, and may use any suitable RAT to facilitate wireless connectivity in local areas such as business locations, homes, vehicles, campuses, industrial facilities, air corridors (e.g., used by drones), roads, and the like. In one embodiment, the base station 114b and the WTRUs 102c, 102d may implement a radio technology (such as IEEE 802.11) to establish a Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN). In an embodiment, the base station 114b and the WTRUs 102c, 102d may implement a radio technology (such as IEEE 802.15) to establish a Wireless Personal Area Network (WPAN). In another embodiment, the base station 114b and the WTRUs 102c, 102d may establish a pico cell or femto cell using a cellular-based RAT (e.g., WCDMA, CDMA2000, GSM, LTE, LTE-A, LTE-a Pro, NR, etc.). As shown in fig. 1A, the base station 114b may have a direct connection with the internet 110. Thus, the base station 114b may not need to access the Internet 110 via the CN 106/115.

The RAN 104/113 may communicate with the CN 106/115, and the CN 106/115 may be any type of network configured to provide voice, data, application, and/or Voice over Internet protocol (VoIP) services to one or more of the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102 d. The data may have varying quality of service (QoS) requirements, such as different throughput requirements, latency requirements, fault tolerance requirements, reliability requirements, data throughput requirements, mobility requirements, and the like. The CN 106/115 may provide call control, billing services, mobile location-based services, prepaid telephony, internet connectivity, video distribution, etc., and/or perform advanced security functions, such as user authentication. Although not shown in fig. 1A, it will be appreciated that the RANs 104/113 and/or CNs 106/115 may communicate directly or indirectly with other RANs that employ the same RAT as the RANs 104/113 or a different RAT. For example, in addition to connecting to the RAN 104/113, which may use NR radio technology, the CN 106/115 may also communicate with another RAN (not shown) employing GSM, UMTS, CDMA 2000, wiMAX, E-UTRA, or WiFi radio technology.

The CN 106/115 may also act as a gateway for the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d to access the PSTN 108, the Internet 110, and/or other networks 112. PSTN 108 may include circuit-switched telephone networks that provide Plain Old Telephone Services (POTS). The internet 110 may include a worldwide interconnecting computer network and device system using common communication protocols, such as Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), user Datagram Protocol (UDP), and/or Internet Protocol (IP) in the TCP/IP internet protocol suite. Network 112 may include wired and/or wireless communication networks owned and/or operated by other service providers. For example, the network 112 may include another CN connected to one or more RANs, which may employ the same RAT as the RANs 104/113 or a different RAT.

Some or all of the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d in the communication system 100 may include multi-mode capabilities (e.g., the WTRUs 102a, 102b, 102c, 102d may include multiple transceivers for communicating with different wireless networks over different wireless links). For example, the WTRU 102c shown in fig. 1A may be configured to communicate with a base station 114a that may employ a cellular-based radio technology and with a base station 114b that may employ an IEEE 802 radio technology.

Fig. 1B is a system diagram illustrating an exemplary WTRU 102. As shown in fig. 1B, the WTRU 102 may include a processor 118, a transceiver 120, a transmit/receive element 122, a speaker/microphone 124, a keypad 126, a display/touchpad 128, non-removable memory 130, removable memory 132, a power source 134, a Global Positioning System (GPS) chipset 136, and/or other peripheral devices 138, etc. It will be appreciated that the WTRU 102 may include any sub-combination of the foregoing elements while remaining consistent with an embodiment.

The processor 118 may be a general purpose processor, a special purpose processor, a conventional processor, a Digital Signal Processor (DSP), a plurality of microprocessors, one or more microprocessors in conjunction with a DSP core, a controller, a microcontroller, an Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) circuit, any other type of Integrated Circuit (IC), a state machine, or the like. The processor 118 may perform signal coding, data processing, power control, input/output processing, and/or any other function that enables the WTRU 102 to operate in a wireless environment. The processor 118 may be coupled to a transceiver 120, and the transceiver 120 may be coupled to a transmit/receive element 122. Although fig. 1B depicts the processor 118 and the transceiver 120 as separate components, it will be appreciated that the processor 118 and the transceiver 120 may be integrated together in an electronic package or chip.

The transmit/receive element 122 may be configured to transmit signals to and receive signals from a base station (e.g., base station 114 a) via the air interface 116. For example, in one embodiment, the transmit/receive element 122 may be an antenna configured to transmit and/or receive RF signals. In an embodiment, for example, the transmit/receive element 122 may be an emitter/detector configured to transmit and/or receive IR, UV, or visible light signals. In another embodiment, the transmit/receive element 122 may be configured to transmit and/or receive both RF and optical signals. It will be appreciated that the transmit/receive element 122 may be configured to transmit and/or receive any combination of wireless signals.

Although the transmit/receive element 122 is depicted as a single element in fig. 1B, the WTRU 102 may include any number of transmit/receive elements 122. More specifically, the WTRU 102 may employ MIMO technology. Thus, in one embodiment, the WTRU 102 may include two or more transmit/receive elements 122 (e.g., multiple antennas) for transmitting and receiving wireless signals over the air interface 116.

The transceiver 120 may be configured to modulate signals to be transmitted by the transmit/receive element 122 and demodulate signals received by the transmit/receive element 122. As described above, the WTRU 102 may have multi-mode capabilities. Thus, the transceiver 120 may include multiple transceivers to enable the WTRU 102 to communicate via multiple RATs (such as, for example, NR and IEEE 802.11).

The processor 118 of the WTRU 102 may be coupled to a speaker/microphone 124, a keypad 126, and/or a display/touchpad 128 (e.g., a Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) display unit or an Organic Light Emitting Diode (OLED) display unit), and may receive user input data from the speaker/microphone 124, the keypad 126, and/or the display/touchpad 128. The processor 118 may also output user data to the speaker/microphone 124, the keypad 126, and/or the display/touchpad 128. In addition, the processor 118 may access information from any type of suitable memory (such as non-removable memory 130 and/or removable memory 132) and store data in the memory. The non-removable memory 130 may include Random Access Memory (RAM), read Only Memory (ROM), a hard disk, or any other type of memory storage device. Removable memory 132 may include a Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) card, a memory stick, a Secure Digital (SD) memory card, and the like. In other embodiments, the processor 118 may never access information from a memory physically located on the WTRU 102, such as on a server or home computer (not shown), and store the data in the memory.

The processor 118 may receive power from the power supply 134 and may be configured to allocate and/or control power to other components in the WTRU 102. The power source 134 may be any suitable device for powering the WTRU 102. For example, the power source 134 may include one or more dry battery packs (e.g., nickel cadmium (NiCd), nickel zinc (NiZn), nickel metal hydride (NiMH), lithium ion (Li-ion), etc.), solar cells, fuel cells, and the like.

The processor 118 may also be coupled to a GPS chipset 136, and the GPS chipset 136 may be configured to provide location information (e.g., longitude and latitude) regarding the current location of the WTRU 102. In addition to or in lieu of information from the GPS chipset 136, the WTRU 102 may receive location information from base stations (e.g., base stations 114a, 114 b) via the air interface 116 and/or determine its location based on the timing of signals being received from two or more nearby base stations. It will be appreciated that the WTRU 102 may obtain location information by any suitable location determination method while remaining consistent with an embodiment.

The processor 118 may be further coupled to other peripheral devices 138, which other peripheral devices 138 may include one or more software and/or hardware modules that provide additional features, functionality, and/or wired or wireless connectivity. For example, the peripheral devices 138 may include an accelerometer, an electronic compass, a satellite transceiver, a digital camera (for photo and/or video), a Universal Serial Bus (USB) port, a vibration device, a television transceiver, a hands-free headset, a Bluetooth (r) module, a Frequency Modulated (FM) radio unit, a digital music player, a media player, a video game player module, an internet browser, a virtual reality and/or augmented reality (VR/AR) device, an activity tracker, and the like. The peripheral device 138 may include one or more sensors, which may be one or more of a gyroscope, an accelerometer, a hall effect sensor, a magnetometer, an orientation sensor, a proximity sensor, a temperature sensor, a time sensor, a geolocation sensor, an altimeter, a light sensor, a touch sensor, a magnetometer, a barometer, a gesture sensor, a biometric sensor, and/or a humidity sensor.

WTRU 102 may include a full duplex radio for which transmission and reception of some or all of the signals (e.g., associated with particular subframes of both UL (e.g., for transmission) and downlink (e.g., for reception)) may be concurrent and/or simultaneous. The full duplex radio may include an interference management unit 139 to reduce and or substantially eliminate self-interference via hardware (e.g., chokes) or via signal processing by a processor (e.g., a separate processor (not shown) or via processor 118). In embodiments, the WTRU 102 may include a half-duplex radio for which some or all of the signals (e.g., associated with a particular subframe of UL (e.g., for transmission) or downlink (e.g., for reception)) are transmitted and received.

A WLAN in infrastructure Basic Service Set (BSS) mode may have an Access Point (AP) for the BSS and one or more Stations (STAs) associated with the AP. An AP may access or have an interface with a Distribution System (DS) or another type of wired/wireless network that carries traffic into and/or out of the BSS. Traffic originating outside the BSS destined for the STA may arrive through the AP and may be delivered to the STA. Traffic originating from the STA destined for a destination outside the BSS may be sent to the AP to be delivered to the corresponding destination. Traffic between STAs within the BSS may be transmitted through the AP, for example, where the source STA may transmit traffic to the AP and the AP may deliver the traffic to the destination STA. Traffic between STAs within a BSS may be considered and/or referred to as peer-to-peer traffic. With Direct Link Setup (DLS), peer-to-peer traffic may be sent between a source and destination STA (e.g., directly between the source and destination STA). In certain representative embodiments, the DLS may use 802.11e DLS or 802.11z Tunnel DLS (TDLS). A WLAN using an Independent BSS (IBSS) mode may not have an AP, and STAs (e.g., all STAs in the STA) within or using the IBSS may communicate directly with each other. The IBSS communication mode may sometimes be referred to herein as an "ad-hoc" communication mode.

When using the 802.11ac infrastructure mode of operation or similar modes of operation, the AP may transmit beacons on a fixed channel (such as a primary channel). The primary channel may be a fixed width (e.g., 20 MHz wide bandwidth) or a dynamically set width via signaling. The primary channel may be an operating channel of the BSS and may be used by the STA to establish a connection with the AP. In some representative embodiments, such as in 802.11 systems, carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance (CSMA/CA) may be implemented. For CSMA/CA, STAs (e.g., each STA), including the AP, may sense the primary channel. If the primary channel is sensed/detected and/or determined to be busy by a particular STA, the particular STA may fall back. In a given BSS, one STA (e.g., only one station) may transmit at any given time.

For example, a High Throughput (HT) STA may communicate using a 40 MHz wide channel via a primary 20MHz channel combined with an adjacent or non-adjacent 20MHz channel to form a 40 MHz wide channel.

Very High Throughput (VHT) STAs may support channels 20 MHz, 40 MHz, 80 MHz and/or 160 MHz wide. By combining adjacent 20 MHz channels, 40 MHz and/or 80 MHz channels can be formed. The 160 MHz channel may be formed by combining 8 contiguous 20 MHz channels, or by combining two non-contiguous 80 MHz channels (this may be referred to as an 80+80 configuration). For the 80+80 configuration, after channel coding, the data may be submitted through a section parser, which may divide the data into two streams. An Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) process and a time domain process may be separately performed for each stream. The streams may be mapped onto two 80 MHz channels and the data may be transmitted by the transmitting STA. At the receiver of the receiving STA, the above-described operations for the 80+80 configuration may be reversed and the combined data may be sent to a Medium Access Control (MAC).

The sub-1 GHz mode of operation is supported by 802.11af and 802.11 ah. In 802.11af and 802.11ah, the channel operating bandwidth and carrier are reduced relative to the channel operating bandwidth and carrier used in 802.11 n and 802.11 ac. The 802.11af supports 5 MHz, 10 MHz, and 20 MHz bandwidths in the TV white space (TVWS) spectrum, and the 802.11ah supports 1 MHz, 2 MHz, 4 MHz, 8 MHz, and 16 MHz bandwidths using non-TVWS spectrum. According to representative embodiments, 802.11ah may support meter type control/machine type communications, such as MTC devices in macro coverage areas. MTC devices may have certain capabilities, such as limited capabilities, including supporting (e.g., supporting only) certain and/or limited bandwidth. MTC devices may include batteries having battery lives above a threshold (e.g., to maintain a very long battery life).

WLAN systems (such as 802.11n, 802.11ac, 802.11af, and 802.11 ah) that can support multiple channels and channel bandwidths include channels that can be designated as primary channels. The primary channel may have a bandwidth equal to the maximum common operating bandwidth supported by all STAs in the BSS. The bandwidth of the primary channel may be set and/or limited by the STA supporting the minimum bandwidth operation mode among all STAs operating in the BSS. In the example of 802.11ah, for STAs (e.g., MTC type devices) that support (e.g., support only) 1 MHz modes, the primary channel may be 1 MHz wide even if APs and other STAs in the BSS support 2 MHz, 4 MHz, 8 MHz, 16 MHz, and/or other channel bandwidth modes of operation. Carrier sensing and/or Network Allocation Vector (NAV) settings may depend on the condition of the primary channel. If the primary channel is busy, for example, due to a STA supporting only 1 MHz modes of operation transmitting to the AP, the entire available frequency band may be considered busy even though most of the frequency band remains idle and possibly available.

Methods and apparatus for obtaining data usable by WTRUs and/or other devices implementing AI and/or ML are described herein. Measurements performed by the WTRU may be used for several purposes, such as scheduling resources for Uplink (UL) and Downlink (DL) transmissions, maintaining serving cells/links (e.g., radio Link Monitoring (RLM), radio link management (RRM)), for mobility decisions (such as handoff, carrier aggregation/dual connectivity (CA/DC), setup/release/change, etc.), etc.

In a Radio Resource Control (RRC) _connected mode, the WTRU may measure one or more beams (at least one) of the cell and the measurement (e.g., power value) may be averaged to derive the cell quality. By doing so, the WTRU may be configured to consider a subset of the detected beams. The filtering may occur, for example, at two different levels, at the physical layer (L1) level to derive beam quality and at the RRC layer (L3) level to derive cell quality from multiple beams. L1 filtering may depend on WTRU implementation and L3 filtering may be configured by the network. By averaging a certain (e.g., configured) number of beams having a signal level above a certain (e.g., configured) threshold, the cell quality may be derived. In the same manner, for one or more serving cells and for one or more non-serving cells, cell quality from beam measurements may be derived. The measurement report may contain the measurement results of the X best beams. The measurement report may be provided by the WTRU if the WTRU is configured to provide the measurement report. The WTRU may be configured to provide the measurement results through any suitable entity (e.g., a network node), such as, for example, through a next generation node B (gNB).

The WTRU may be configured with at least one measurement object for each measurement type to be performed. The measurement object may specify what is to be measured. For example, the measurement object may include, but is not limited to, any suitable combination of information such as, for example, synchronization signal block/channel state information-reference signal (SSB/CSI-RS) resource configuration (e.g., frequency, timing (e.g., SSB-based RRM measurement timing configuration (SMTC) window)), subcarrier spacing, list of cells (allowed cells, forbidden cells, etc.), minimum beam quality to be considered during cell quality derivation, number of beams to be averaged for cell quality derivation, measurement quantity (e.g., reference Signal Received Power (RSRP), radio Signal Received Quality (RSRQ), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)), and the like.

The measurement object may be associated with one or more reporting configurations (e.g., via a measurement Identifier (ID)), where the reporting configurations may be event-triggered or periodic. If it is periodic, the WTRU may send a measurement report at each reporting interval (the reporting interval may be in a range between 120 milliseconds (ms) and 30 minutes (min), for example).

For event-triggered measurements, the WTRU may send a measurement report when conditions associated with the event are fulfilled. The WTRU may continuously measure the serving cell and neighbor report amounts and validate it with a threshold or offset defined in the reporting configuration. The reporting amount may be RSRP, RSRQ, signal-to-interference-and-noise ratio (SINR), etc., or any suitable combination thereof.

The measurement report may contain the cell quality of the serving and/or neighbor cell and, together with the cell quality, the X best beams of that cell may be included. The WTRU may be configured to provide the measurement report through any suitable entity, such as, for example, through the gNB.

Measurement events may include intra-radio access technology (intra-RAT) events and inter-RAT events. Exemplary intra-RAT events may include events A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, and A6, as described below.

Event A1 may indicate that a particular measurement object of the serving cell is becoming better than a threshold. Event A1 may trigger cancellation of an ongoing handoff procedure. This may be applicable if the WTRU moves towards the cell edge and triggers a mobility procedure, but then moves back into good coverage before the mobility procedure has completed.

Event A2 may indicate that a particular measurement object of the serving cell is becoming worse than a threshold. Event A2 may not involve any neighbor cell measurements. Event A2 may be used to trigger a blind mobility procedure. When the network receives the measurement report triggered by event A2, the network may configure the WTRU for neighbor cell measurements in order to save WTRU battery (e.g., neighbor cell measurements are not performed when the serving cell quality is good enough).

Event A3 may indicate that a particular measurement object of a neighbor cell is becoming better than that of a special cell (SpCell). Event A3 may be used to trigger a handoff procedure. Note that SpCell is a primary serving cell (e.g., primary cell (PCell)) of a primary cell group (MCG) or a primary serving cell (e.g., primary secondary serving cell (PSCell)) of a Secondary Cell Group (SCG). Thus, in Dual Connectivity (DC) operation, the Secondary Node (SN) can configure an A3 event for Secondary Node (SN) -triggered PSCell changes. Event A3 may be used in conjunction with Conditional Handoff (CHO) or conditional PSCell changes.

Event A4 may indicate that a particular measurement object of a neighbor cell is becoming better than a threshold. Event A4 may be used to trigger a serving cell coverage independent handover procedure (e.g., load balancing, where the WTRU is handed over to a good neighbor cell even if serving cell conditions are excellent).

Event A5 may indicate that a particular measurement object of the SpCell is becoming worse than a first threshold (threshold 1) and that the particular measurement object of the neighbor cell is becoming better than a second threshold (threshold 2). Similar to event A3, event A5 may be used to trigger a handoff, but unlike event A3, event A5 may provide a handoff trigger mechanism based on absolute measurements of serving and neighbor cells, while event A3 uses a relative comparison. Event A5 may be suitable for time critical handoffs when the serving cell is weaker and must change towards another cell that may not meet the criteria for event A3 handoff.

Event A6 may indicate that a particular measurement object of a neighbor cell is becoming better than a particular quality of the SCell by an offset. Event A6 may be used for SCell addition/release.

Example inter-RAT events may include events B1 and B2, as described herein. Event B1 may indicate that a particular quality of an inter-RAT neighbor cell is becoming better than a threshold. Event B1 is similar to event A4, but for the case of inter-RAT handover. Event B2 may indicate that a particular measurement object of the PCell is becoming worse than threshold1 and that the particular measurement object of the inter-RAT neighbor is becoming better than threshold2. Event B2 is similar to event A5, but for the case of inter-RAT handover.

Fig. 3 is an exemplary depiction of a conditional handoff configuration and execution. The concepts of Conditional Handover (CHO) and conditional PSCell addition/change (CPA/CPC or collectively CPAC) are introduced in NR to reduce the likelihood of Radio Link Failure (RLF) and handover failure (HOF). The handover may be triggered by the measurement report even though no factor prevents the network from sending a HO command to the WTRU if the WTRU does not receive the measurement report. For example, the WTRU may be configured with an A3 event, the A3 event triggering measurement report is sent when the radio signal level/quality (RSRP, RSRQ, etc.) of the neighbor cell becomes better than the primary serving cell (PCell) (or primary secondary serving cell (PSCell) in the case of Dual Connectivity (DC)). The WTRU may monitor the serving and neighbor cells and may send measurement reports when conditions are met. When such a report is received, the network (current serving node/cell) may prepare the HO command (basically, RRC reconfiguration message with reconfigurationWithSync) and may send it to the WTRU, which may immediately execute the HO command, resulting in the WTRU connecting to the target cell.

CHO differs from traditional handoffs in at least two respects. In CHO, multiple handoff targets are prepared (as compared to only one target in the conventional case). In CHO, the WTRU does not perform CHO immediately as in the case of conventional handover. Alternatively, the WTRU may be configured with a trigger condition (such as a set of radio conditions), and the WTRU may perform a handoff toward one of the targets only if/only the trigger condition is met.

While radio conditions towards the current serving cell are still good, CHO commands may be sent, thereby reducing two points of failure in conventional handoffs, such as the risk of failing to send measurement reports (e.g., if the link quality of the current serving cell drops below an acceptable level when the measurement report is triggered in normal handoffs) and failing to receive the handoff commands (e.g., if the link quality of the current serving cell drops below an acceptable level after the WTRU has sent the measurement report but before it has received the HO command).

The CHO trigger condition may also be based on the radio quality of the serving cell and neighbor cells, such as the conditions used to trigger measurement reports in conventional NR/LTE. For example, the WTRU (302) may be configured (304) with CHO with trigger conditions and associated HO commands like A3. The WTRU may monitor (306) the current and serving cells and when the A3 trigger condition is met, instead of sending a measurement report, it may perform an associated HO command (308) and switch its connection towards the target cell.

Another benefit of CHO is that it helps to prevent unnecessary re-establishment in case of radio link failure. For example, assume that a WTRU is configured with multiple CHO targets and the WTRU experiences a Radio Link Failure (RLF) before the trigger condition of any of the targets is met. Conventional operation would result in an RRC re-establishment procedure that would result in a significant interruption time of the WTRU's bearers. However, in the case of CHO, if after RLF is detected, the WTRU is eventually located in the cell (the WTRU has CHO associated with the cell) (e.g., the target cell is already ready for the WTRU), the WTRU may directly perform the HO command associated with this target cell instead of continuing to perform the full re-establishment procedure.

CPC and CPA are extensions of CHO, but in DC scenarios. The WTRU can be configured with a trigger condition for a PSCell change or addition, and when the trigger condition is met, it may execute an associated PSCell change or PSCell addition command. Additional events for conditional handoff may include conditional event A3 (CondEvent A), conditional event A4 (CondEvent A4), and conditional event A5 (CondEvent A5). Manual (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) operations are based on models (e.g., neural networks) that have been trained using large amounts of data under different scenarios/conditions. For a given function, there may be several models (e.g., each model trained/adapted for different network/WTRU conditions/characteristics). For example, mechanisms and frameworks may be specified to use AI/ML-based schemes for air interface levels (e.g., CSI feedback enhancement (e.g., CSI compression), beam management, and WTRU positioning) as well as network levels (e.g., network power saving, load balancing, and mobility).

As used herein, the term AI/ML (artificial intelligence/machine learning) describes any model and/or associated learning algorithm used by a WTRU, network, device, etc. to predict future behavior (e.g., behavior at the WTRU that is about to be sent to or from the network to the WTRU of the data arrival rate/amount). The model and associated learning algorithm are assumed to use a large dataset that may be collected by the WTRU and/or the network. Further, it may be assumed that the AI/ML model is predicting based on several conditions, such as current time, current WTRU location, WTRU mobility pattern, etc. For example, based on current and/or historical measurements of UL/DL data arrival/quantity, the AI/ML model may be able to predict future UL/DL data arrival (e.g., consider UL/DL data arrival rate/quantity at a time of day similar to the current time/place or/and at a place similar to the current time/place, consider currently active bearers/applications, etc.).

As described herein, the terms Artificial Intelligence (AI), machine Learning (ML), deep Learning (DL), DNN may be used interchangeably. Although the techniques described herein are illustrated based on learning in a wireless communication system, they may additionally or alternatively be used in other systems including, for example, any type of transmission, communication system, and/or service, etc.

The techniques and mechanisms described herein for data collection enhancement are independent with respect to the AI/ML model/technique being used (e.g., the algorithm used, the mechanism such as the neural network or which neural network, e.g., depth and parameters/weights of the network, etc.). However, the WTRU may have a pre-trained AI/ML model that can generate predictions of UL/DL data arrival rate/amount.

The predictions may be associated with one point in time (e.g., X ms from now on, the model yields the desired UL/DL data arrival rate/amount), or may extend over several time steps (e.g., a time series prediction for the next Y ms, at each X ms interval, etc.). The AI/ML model located on the WTRU may be implementation-based (e.g., installed/provided by the WTRU vendor), or the WTRU may obtain the AI/ML model from the network.

For any predicted value, the predicted value itself may be associated with and/or represented by a confidence or error tolerance value, and may be represented by an average, peak, minimum, etc. along a short time window representing the validity of the prediction. The WTRU may communicate with the network regarding AI/ML capabilities (e.g., where the WTRU may be able to indicate to the network the AI/ML model/function that is supported, a confidence level of the prediction, e.g., a predicted period of time (how long the prediction is to be made for the future), etc.). The WTRU may support several AI/ML models for a certain function (e.g., with different prediction periods, prediction confidence levels, processing requirements, trained under/for operation in different cell/location/time of day/application types, etc.). A given AI/ML model may operate in different modes (e.g., with different levels of prediction confidence in different prediction periods, etc.). The WTRU may select an AI/ML model for a certain function (e.g., the network decides for which functions the WTRU is able to use AI/ML based operation and the WTRU may select the AI/ML model to use) or the network may explicitly control this (e.g., the WTRU provides details about the AI/ML model and its capabilities, the network determines which model to activate for a particular function).

The AI/ML model may exist at the WTRU and have been trained, or the WTRU may be provided with an untrained AI/ML model and perform the training itself. The AI/ML model may exist at the WTRU and have been trained, and the WTRU may be enabled/configured to perform further training (e.g., for different conditions such as cell/location/time of day, etc., for conditions other than initial training, for the same conditions as initial training, but for increasing confidence levels or/and prediction periods, etc.).

In the case of time series outputs, the prediction confidence may vary from output to output (e.g., confidence level of predictions for X ms is higher compared to predictions for Y ms, where Y > X, etc.). The prediction confidence level may have a percentage confidence (e.g., the expected likelihood of this prediction will be true), in terms of error margin (e.g., in Y ms, the predicted UL data rate is expected to be between X-lower_error_margin and x+upper_error_margin), or both a confidence percentage and an error margin (e.g., in Z ms, the predicted UL data rate is expected to be between X-lower-error_margin and x+upper_error_ magin, with 90% confidence). For a given prediction period, there may be different ranges of prediction values with different confidence levels or error margins (e.g., in Y ms, the predicted UL data rate is expected to be between X1-lower_error_margin1 and X1+ upper_error_margin1 with 95% confidence; between X2-lower_error_margin2 and X2+ upper_error_margin2 with 85% confidence; etc.).

The perceptron is an NN that includes a function that multiplies its input by learned weight coefficients to produce an output value. A feed-forward NN is an NN that receives input at one or more nodes of an input layer and moves information in a direction through one or more hidden layers to one or more nodes of an output layer. NR has a mechanism for measuring radio conditions while the WTRU is IDLE/INACTIVE/CONNECTED, recording them while IDLE/INACTIVE, and reporting measurements while CONNECTED (reporting recorded measurements when CONNECTED state is entered, or reporting instant measurements performed in CONNECTED state when certain event is met or periodically).

However, with respect to the Radio Resource Management (RRM) and MDT framework of NR in the context of AI/ML model training and performance monitoring, in CONNECTED state, measurement logging is not supported. Since only the beam integration of a certain number of best beams (e.g. beams with a radio quality above a certain threshold) of a given cell is considered, it is not possible to "track" the quality of the beam over a certain duration. Each sample of the beam/cell that records the measurement, or even the L3 filtered measurement, may be overburdened (e.g., at the memory requirements of the WTRU) and some of the recorded data may be irrelevant to the task at hand. Measurements performed for RRM purposes may be inadequate for model training or performance training purposes because the network may configure the WTRU with as few measurements as possible that are expected to be adequate for normal operation (e.g., the WTRU is configured to measure only a few neighbor cells/frequencies). If extensive logging is performed by the WTRU, most of the logged data may be irrelevant to model training or performance monitoring, e.g., for performance monitoring, measurements performed only for a certain duration before and after taking action (e.g., since the AI/ML function is autonomously taken by the WTRU, triggered by the network, etc.) may be sufficient. The various embodiments discussed below address these shortcomings.

In various example embodiments, a WTRU may be configured to perform logging of beam/cell measurements for one or more cells, where the configuration may include conditions for determining when to start/stop logging, cell/beam identities to be logged, conditions for determining which measurements are to be included in the logging (e.g., conditions for determining whether to log an entry), perform measurement logging, send an indication of the availability of the logged measurements, and send a report under certain conditions (e.g., receiving a request/grant from a network). For example, the first condition associated with when to begin recording may relate to a likelihood of occurrence of at least one first event within the first time period. The WTRU may perform the measurements and analyze the measurement results. The WTRU may begin recording additional measurements if the measurement indicates that the likelihood of the at least one event occurring within the first time period equals or exceeds a threshold. The second condition associated with when to stop recording may relate to a likelihood that the at least one second event has occurred within a second time period. The WTRU may stop recording measurements based on determining that the likelihood that the at least one event has occurred within the second time period exceeds a second threshold. The WTRU may then send a report including an indication of the recorded measurements.
